title: There are many 5-holes
summary: Given a set P of points on the plane, a polygon with vertices in P is said to be empty if it contains no element of P in its interior. We show that every set of n points in general position on the plane determines at least $Ω(n^{20/11})$ empty convex pentagons (also known as 5-holes). This result improves upon the previous bound of $Ω(n\cdot(\log n)^{4/5})$ obtained by Aicholzer et al. [JCT A, 2020], and significantly narrows the gap with respect to the conjectured $Ω(n^2)$ lower bound (which, if true, would be tight).
